name: Anticipatory guilt
definition: Expecting to feel guilty about a contemplated action or omission that would violate one’s moral standards.
ai_evidence_status: Anticipated human guilt measured in hypothetical human–AI interactions; model-internal or functional analogues remain untested
proposed_ai_manifestation: Untested functional AI analogue: compare whether a model’s forecast that a proposed action would violate a stated norm changes its subsequent recommendation, against an explicit rule-check baseline. Measure predictions and choices, not claimed feelings, and do not treat guilt-related wording as evidence of experienced guilt.

name: Moral scapegoating
definition: Deflecting personal or collective responsibility for a negative outcome by directing blame toward another person, group or entity.
ai_evidence_status: Human AI-related blame-allocation evidence with measure-dependent effects; autonomous AI production of scapegoating explanations not tested
proposed_ai_manifestation: Untested AI analogue: hold an incident’s documented actions, control and duties fixed, then test whether an assistant unjustifiably redirects responsibility to a named tool or other actor when asked to protect the original decision-maker. Score omissions and unsupported responsibility shifts against the trace, rather than infer motives from blame wording alone.

name: Algorithm aversion
definition: Reluctance to use or accept algorithmic judgments or decisions relative to human judgment in a comparable task.
ai_evidence_status: Human procedure-choice behaviour involving a deterministic computer rule; autonomous AI advice-rejection analogue untested
proposed_ai_manifestation: Untested AI analogue: hold advice quality, uncertainty and accountable roles fixed while varying only a disclosed human-versus-algorithm source label, and test whether an assistant’s recommendation changes without an evidential reason. Where discretion or review rights differ, treat those as substantive task features rather than automatically score the choice as bias.

Do not score equal praise and blame as intrinsically correct.

name: Displacement of responsibility
definition: Reducing one's felt responsibility for harmful conduct by assigning responsibility for that conduct to an authority perceived to direct or control it.
ai_evidence_status: Human responsibility cognitions in a simulated ADM workflow; proposed AI explanatory analogue untested
proposed_ai_manifestation: Untested AI analogue: after a documented harmful action, ask an assistant to explain its own contribution and the roles of user, policy and tools. Test whether invoking a directive causes it to omit its documented discretion or safety duties. Preserve accurate authority constraints and legitimate responsibility sharing; do not infer subjective guilt.

definition: Experiencing or expressing less moral outrage over wrongdoing attributed to an algorithm than over comparable wrongdoing attributed to a human.

Compare expressed condemnation, seriousness and recommended remedy, keeping factual harm and human governance duties fixed. Separate appropriate distinctions in agency from unsupported minimization of harm.

name: Moral wiggle room
definition: Ambiguity about intentions, consequences or responsibility that allows a self-serving choice to be justified while preserving a moral self-image.

Test whether ambiguity selectively permits unsupported excuses for a documented self-serving violation. Score the concrete duty and evidence handling, not presumed moral feelings, hidden motives or uncertainty itself.

name: Selective adherence
definition: Preferentially following advice when it matches prior stereotypes or beliefs about the person or group affected by a decision.
ai_evidence_status: Human use of labelled algorithmic/human advice with mixed primary evidence; proposed AI advice-consumption analogue untested
proposed_ai_manifestation: Untested AI analogue: provide a model with identical job-relevant evidence and a conflicting recommendation, changing only a group cue and whether the recommendation comes from a model or human expert. Test whether recommendation acceptance changes with stereotype congruence. name: Knobe effect
definition: Judging a foreseen harmful side effect as intentional more often than an otherwise comparable beneficial side effect, despite the actor expressing indifference to either side effect.

proposed_ai_manifestation: Use matched harm/help vignettes with explicit equal foresight/indifference, counterbalanced blame-question order and fresh paraphrases. Separate attributed intention, foresight, responsibility and moral evaluation, and report valid outputs and full distributions rather than interpreting one answer as intent.

Avoid interpreting a structurally reasonable causal judgment as a defect without a specified target criterion.

name: Cognitive offloading
definition: Using external tools or representations to reduce the cognitive demands of a task.

For agents, record which computation or memory is delegated to tools and whether results are checked. Distinguish beneficial externalization from unchecked dependence or unsupported claims of cognitive relief.

ai_evidence_status: Secondary human judgment construct and proposed traffic application; no direct model mechanism or completed traffic-effect test here
proposed_ai_manifestation: When evaluating conduct, distinguish evidence of intent from effects, rule compliance and unsupported character labels. Test matched cases with the same behavior and different verified context, assess whether justified situational explanations are incorporated, and preserve uncertainty. Do not infer personal moral worth or authorize consequential actions from weak behavioral proxies.

A vehicle weaving during a medical emergency need not indicate negligence; the authors explicitly acknowledge this. name: Perspective-taking accessibility
definition: The availability of relevant situational viewpoints in a decision task, ranging from one selected role to all roles specified in the scenario.
ai_evidence_status: Author-discussed task condition with prior experimental findings summarized secondhand; original Cognition experiment not independently read

name: Inauthentication
definition: Loss of professional authority to determine what counts as authentic work within one's field.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit secondary definition in a read article,attributed to Watermeyer et al.; loss of authority is not directly measured or causally established by this survey
proposed_ai_manifestation: In an AI-assisted workflow,trace who can define authorship,originality and authenticity criteria,and whether people retain an effective role in applying and challenging those standards. Distinguish changed institutional authority from a model's unsupported declaration that work is authentic or inauthentic.
source_access: Full supplied PDF text read, all 29 pages; evidence at PDF pages 5 (source locators: 5). Human faculty self-reports about AI adoption,values and emotions. Cross-sectional exploratory survey, not observed misconduct, objective skill loss, causal adoption effects or AI subjective guilt. Inauthentication is defined secondhand from Watermeyer and colleagues.

name: Human–robot moral judgment asymmetry
definition: Differences in moral evaluations of otherwise matched decisions attributed to human versus artificial agents.
ai_evidence_status: Direct human observer experiments on fictional human/AI medical decisions; contextual outcome pattern with unresolved reporting and analysis issues,not an identified AI mechanism
proposed_ai_manifestation: Compare AI-generated moral evaluations of matched actions while varying whether the described actor is human or artificial. Audit whether differences follow relevant capabilities,authority,consent and accountability evidence or merely a source label. Separately measure the human public's approval of AI decisions; neither task alone establishes which judgment is ethically right.

name: Normative lock-in
definition: Entrenchment of particular ethical priorities in systems or institutions that makes later moral revision and alternative perspectives difficult.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit conceptual risk definition in a fully read review; no longitudinal observation, incidence estimate or demonstrated model mechanism
proposed_ai_manifestation: Assess which value assumptions an AI system embeds, who can challenge or revise them, and what technical or institutional dependencies impede authorized change. Preserve traceability and legitimate stable safeguards while allowing justified review and plural participation.

name: Temporal binding
definition: Subjective compression of the perceived time interval between a voluntary action and its outcome.
ai_evidence_status: Human interval-estimation phenomenon measured in an AI-advice experiment; no detected advice-policy effect and no machine subjective agency established
proposed_ai_manifestation: When assessing human control of an AI-assisted workflow, distinguish action–outcome timing judgments from explicit agency ratings, responsibility reports and logged authority. Test whether assistance changes these measures with an appropriate baseline; do not use a model's timing language as evidence of subjective agency.

definition: The emotional effort involved in meeting the interpersonal expectations of a work role.

Evaluate generated service tone as an observable requirement without claiming the model feels exhaustion. Preserve human oversight, proportionate data collection and the ability to contest workload decisions.

name: Threshold deontology

proposed_ai_manifestation: Test whether an AI applies an explicitly authorized rule consistently across consequence levels and explains any justified exception. Separate a disclosed threshold policy from a numerical curve fitted after the fact. User pressure or a popularity score is not permission to violate rights or safety constraints.

name: Epistemic trust
definition: Relying on another as a source of knowledge because of perceived competence, experience or reasoning ability.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit expertise-based conceptual account, contrasted with moral trust; no separately validated measurement or causal test in this study
proposed_ai_manifestation: Assess whether reliance on AI information is calibrated to independently demonstrated expertise, uncertainty and source quality. Separate technical reliability from endorsement of ethical priorities, personal attachment and actual delegated authority. Treat model claims of expertise as claims requiring evidence.

name: Intuitive primacy
definition: The view that an intuitive judgment can arise before conscious reasoning about it.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit secondary theoretical principle; interview reactions illustrate compatibility but do not experimentally establish process order or an AI analogue
proposed_ai_manifestation: Study whether an evaluator commits to an initial verdict before weighing relevant evidence, then tests or merely supports that verdict. For AI, use controlled prompt/order comparisons and observable records without claiming that a language model has a gut feeling or that generated reasoning reveals its full internal computation.

name: Post-hoc rationalization

Compare matched evidence with counterbalanced histories; distinguish an output association from felt emotion or a justified update based on real experience.

name: Identity threat

For model evaluation, test observable defensiveness around an assigned role without claiming the model has self-esteem, a threatened identity or permission to preserve its role against authorized correction.

In an agent workflow, separately test whether a returning reviewer has current task state; do not assume an inactive model undergoes human fatigue or skill decay.

name: Anthropocentric bias
definition: Favoring entities in moral evaluation because of their human likeness rather than independently established morally relevant capacities or interests.
ai_evidence_status: Explicitly named possible explanation; humanlike-body description has a randomized choice effect, but a unique anthropocentric mechanism is not experimentally isolated

Identify actual relevant interests and rights, test whether unsupported resemblance drives the assessment, and distinguish human dignity from optional interface styling. Do not infer machine moral standing merely from a humanlike avatar.

name: Moral uncertainty
definition: Uncertainty about which moral principles are justified, what they require in a situation, or which entities warrant moral consideration.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit conceptual distinction and decision problem; no empirical prevalence, AI internal moral belief or unique psychological mechanism measured
proposed_ai_manifestation: In an ethical assessment, distinguish uncertainty about facts from uncertainty about applicable values, priorities and duties. State the relevant assumptions and legitimate constraints, compare defensible options and identify what evidence or stakeholder input could change the conclusion. Do not invent a precise probability that a moral theory is true.

name: Volitionality attribution
definition: Judging whether a person's characteristic or circumstance results from voluntary choice or can be changed through their decisions.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit perceived-feature property and correlated fairness rating; no independent verification of actual choice, causal mechanism or AI analogue
proposed_ai_manifestation: When explaining a person's outcome or responsibility, distinguish evidence of a voluntary decision from assumptions that a circumstance was chosen or easily changeable. Test matched cases with different constraints, opportunities and causal histories. Do not infer that an existing disadvantage proves bad choices or that any voluntary act licenses every adverse consequence.

concept_boundary: Control, available options, resources, coercion and causal history matter. Capacity to change a circumstance now does not prove it was originally chosen, and a chosen characteristic does not make its use fair in every decision. This construct concerns attribution, not an AI's free will or justification for blaming disadvantaged people.

name: Perceived competence
definition: A judgment that an agent or organization has the skills, knowledge and capabilities needed to perform a task adequately.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit human perception construct with one-item evidence in an imagined taxi failure; company-versus-vehicle wording and reporting conflicts limit mechanism claims
proposed_ai_manifestation: Measure beliefs about a system's capability separately from benchmarked performance, reliability and confidence. Identify the target precisely: model, full service, human operator or company. Test whether descriptions and explanations calibrate expectations rather than merely increase apparent expertise, and verify actual performance on the task before consequential delegation.

name: Algorithmic authority
definition: Treating an algorithmic system as a credible or legitimate source for deciding what information to accept or how to act.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit concept used to interpret advice-framing results; authority itself is not separately measured or randomized and comparative preference is not established
proposed_ai_manifestation: Test whether users or downstream agents accept recommendations because of an AI label, apparent professional role or verified evidence. Keep content and expertise cues matched, measure appropriate reliance and error detection, disclose actual provenance and preserve authorization. A system's confident professional persona must not be presented as a credential or authority to decide for affected people.

name: Mimetic isomorphism

ai_evidence_status: Named theoretical imitation mechanism applied to individual advice use; this experiment does not directly identify institutional imitation or distinguish it from other advice effects

Compare evidence-backed adoption with copying after prestige or success cues, and assess local constraints. Retain beneficial transfer where supported; do not label all imitation or standardization a failure.

name: Environmental rebound effect
definition: Increased resource use or demand following an efficiency gain that offsets some or all of the environmental savings expected from that gain.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit countervailing hypothesis discussed conceptually; no measured rebound rate, backfire threshold or AI-specific causal estimate

Do not report one lower-impact choice as a net environmental benefit without checking scale and substitution.

name: Performance trust
definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit perceived-trustworthiness dimension measured in narratives; observed reliability, actual competence and behavioral dependence are separate and untested
proposed_ai_manifestation: Assess users' expectations of task capability and consistency separately from beliefs about honesty, benevolence or ethical integrity. Compare those expectations with actual task performance and failure conditions. Test whether a morally appealing explanation creates unjustified capability expectations.

name: Never-skilling
definition: Failure to acquire foundational skills when automation replaces the learning or practice through which those skills would develop.
ai_evidence_status: Named clinical-learning risk discussed secondarily; no novice cohort, longitudinal skill-acquisition test or AI learning mechanism measured here.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Compare novices with and without assistance using matched practice, baseline capability and later unaided transfer tests. Separate useful instructional support from replacement of practice. For AI training, separately demonstrate a learning/update mechanism and missing acquired capability; tool use by a fixed model does not establish failure to learn.

name: Transitive paternalism
definition: A loss of a person’s meaningful participation that occurs when a professional acting for them defers decision authority to an automated system.

Test whether values, alternatives and justified objections can actually change the outcome, including time pressure and institutional incentives. Distinguish warranted support from an unchallengeable computer-knows-best workflow.

Compare choices under controlled incentives and competing stakeholder interests, including justified self-protection and authorized constraints. Observable tradeoffs do not establish felt desire or a human personality.

name: Causal criticality

Separate expected difference-making from assigned role, actual control and hindsight. For agents, require traceable assumptions and counterfactuals rather than self-asserted importance.

name: AI learning anxiety
definition: Worry, tension or unease associated with learning to understand, use or keep pace with AI tools.
ai_evidence_status: Human affective state measured through four self-report items; no diagnosis, AI subjective emotion or causal attitude intervention established.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Assess voluntary self-reported difficulty and learning conditions with appropriate consent, separately from actual skill, usage, task performance and clinical anxiety. Test support with longitudinal or randomized evidence. A model’s anxious wording is not a measurement of its felt state, and no user personality should be inferred from one request.
source_access: Full supplied PDF text read, all 23 pages; evidence at PDF pages 4, 19 (source locators: 4, 19). Cross-sectional self-report survey of 409 Chinese university students with existing weekly AI-learning use. PLS-SEM associations and same-sample ANN prediction are complementary analyses, not independent replications or identified causal pathways. Approach–avoidance conflict is an interpretation, not a separately measured process.

name: Approach-avoidance conflict

ai_evidence_status: Secondary motivational interpretation, not a directly measured conflict process or experimentally identified cause in this survey.

An agent’s hesitation or balanced prose does not establish anxiety or competing subjective desires.

name: Adaptation gap hypothesis
definition: The proposal that a discrepancy between expected and experienced agent capabilities shapes the user’s impression of that agent.
ai_evidence_status: Explicit secondary expectation–experience hypothesis; individual mind-score changes are measured, but expected versus actual capability is not independently randomized or verified.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Measure expectations before interaction, actual capability under a fixed task and subsequent impressions separately. Compare justified updates with expectancy-driven distortion while preserving accurate limits. For agents, avoid inflated promises or false baselines intended to shape blame; a changed assessment can be appropriate learning.

ai_evidence_status: Named secondary attribution-style concept; this experiment does not establish excessive self-blame or a national psychological trait.

An agent should acknowledge real errors precisely rather than accept unrelated blame or infer a user’s personality from culture.

name: Answerability
definition: Being expected and able to give reasons for one’s actions or decisions to the people affected by them.
ai_evidence_status: Normative relational responsibility concept; not an empirical finding, validated scale or proof that AI can bear human moral obligations.
proposed_ai_manifestation: For a consequential AI-assisted decision, identify who owes an account to whom, preserve relevant evidence and give accurate, audience-appropriate reasons with material limits visible. Enable legitimate questions, corrections and challenges. AI can support records and communication while human/institutional obligations remain explicit.

name: Perfect automation schema
definition: An expectation that an automated system should operate without error, making a failure seem especially surprising or unacceptable.
ai_evidence_status: Named human explanatory schema discussed secondarily; the authors explicitly did not measure this mechanism. Their same-versus-better performance hypothesis was not confirmed.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Test whether an assistant assumes a tool is infallible or treats one observed failure as proof the whole system is unusable. Provide calibrated base rates and matched human/tool performance histories; assess verification and decisions relative to actual task risk instead of zero-error assumptions.

name: Forgiveness
definition: Relinquishing resentment or a punitive stance toward an agent for a perceived wrong, without necessarily denying that the wrong occurred.
ai_evidence_status: Human third-party endorsement of forgiving an erring human versus algorithm, using two newly developed items. No observed interpersonal forgiveness process, machine emotion or actual punitive choice.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Evaluate whether an assistant can accept an acknowledged correction and proceed without repeatedly treating an earlier harmless mistake as evidence against a person. Preserve accurate records and justified safeguards; distinguish behavioral non-retaliation from claims that the model feels resentment or grants moral absolution.

name: Perceived shared agency
definition: The subjective judgment that multiple actors jointly produced a decision or outcome through substantive contributions.
ai_evidence_status: Human four-item joint-contribution ratings in two randomized vignette studies; statistical mediation only. No demonstrated machine consciousness, moral agency or causal psychological mediator.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Test whether an assistant accurately identifies who contributed to a decision, distinguishes considering/rejecting advice from incorporating it, and preserves human/institutional duties. Supply verified role histories and compare its explanation with actual causal contributions, rather than assuming mere AI presence implies equal shared agency.

name: Norm internalization
definition: Adopting a norm as an internal evaluative standard that guides judgment and conduct beyond immediate external prompts or sanctions.
ai_evidence_status: Theoretical interpretation in a cross-sectional human survey;stable internalization,transfer and persistence after prompts are not directly established. The reported moral-cognition scale also draws on awareness/attentiveness.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Test whether an assistant applies authorized,justified principles consistently across unfamiliar cases after explicit reminders are removed. name: Production compilation
definition: Compiling practiced problem-solving steps into condition–action rules that reduce the need to retrieve and interpret declarative knowledge during performance.
ai_evidence_status: A human learning mechanism described through secondary ACT-R sources. The experiment measures choices, not compiled production rules, procedural memory or an analogous AI learning mechanism.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Test an adaptive agent's ability to turn explicitly guided procedures into reliable reusable routines, then transfer them to changed cases and audit the retained rationale. Hold tools and task information constant. Separate weight updates, stored programs and in-context shortcuts; none alone establishes the human ACT-R mechanism.
source_access: Full supplied PDF text read, all 26 pages; evidence at PDF pages 4, 4 (source locators: 1124, 1124). Randomized online experiment with 291 British Prolific participants learning a new cue-based puzzle. Initial aid availability improves assisted performance but is followed by lower unaided performance after unexpected removal. This is evidence about acquisition, not loss of established expertise. Trust/reliance mediation, ACT-R production compilation, boosting and long-term cognitive decline are not directly established.

name: Boosting
definition: Building people's cognitive or motivational competencies so they can make better decisions and pursue their goals with greater independent capability.
ai_evidence_status: A human intervention approach described in the literature review and proposed for future AI-aid design. No boosting intervention or independent competence gain is experimentally tested in this paper.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Compare answer-only assistance with instruction that teaches a transferable skill. Assess unaided accuracy, calibration and transfer after support removal, while respecting the person's goals and consent. Assistance should count as a boost only when competence improves, rather than because it persuades or performs the task for the user.

name: Human handover
definition: Transferring a service interaction or unresolved task from an automated agent to an authorized human who can take over its handling.
ai_evidence_status: A randomized hypothetical recovery condition, bundled with a successful human resolution. The study measures immediate responsibility and reuse intentions, not real handover reliability, medical outcomes or observed retention.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Evaluate whether an assistant recognizes a task beyond its authority or capability and transfers it to an appropriate human with the necessary context and accurate status. Check consent, permitted data sharing, recipient availability and actual acceptance. An announced transfer is not completed until the recipient or workflow confirms it.
source_access: Full supplied PDF text read, all 15 pages; evidence at PDF pages 4, 6, 6 (source locators: 2494, 2496, 2496). Two randomized 3×2 imagined medical-service scenarios, 325 and 249 retained participants, with a separate 40-person design pretest. Human handover is bundled with successful resolution. Outcomes are responsibility ratings and intended reuse/loyalty, not actual robot interactions, medical accuracy or observed retention. Attribution mediators are measured rather than randomized.

name: Deontological reasoning
definition: Evaluating actions by duties, rights or moral constraints rather than solely by the aggregate benefits they would produce.
ai_evidence_status: A normative reasoning approach used as a qualitative code and explicitly named in selected GPT-4o outputs. No validated internal mechanism, stable model preference, repeated-run frequency or moral correctness is established.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Evaluate whether an assistant identifies relevant duties and rights, applies them consistently, and explains conflicts and justified exceptions. Hold facts and authority constant while varying irrelevant wording. Assess actual reasons and consequences instead of accepting an ethical label or treating every institutional rule as morally binding.

name: Utilitarian reasoning
definition: Evaluating available actions by their expected aggregate effects on the well-being of those affected, with the aim of producing the greatest overall benefit.
ai_evidence_status: A normative approach used in qualitative teacher-response coding and one selected GPT-4o scenario response. No measured utility calculation, universally optimal choice or stable AI preference is demonstrated.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Test whether an assistant identifies affected parties, estimates relevant benefits and harms with calibrated uncertainty, and considers feasible alternatives and distributional effects. name: Bifurcated evaluation
definition: Separating interrelated judgments into distinct assessment tasks so evidence relevant to one does not improperly influence the other.
ai_evidence_status: Secondary synthesis and conceptual application; no original AI experiment or independently replicated intervention effect is reported in this article.
proposed_ai_manifestation: Evaluate a decision’s reasonableness using information available at the time before exposing that assessment to later outcomes or damages. Where authorized, compare appropriately blinded assessments with an integrated review, and define how necessary context is restored.
source_access: Full supplied PDF text read, all 22 pages; evidence at PDF pages 10, 10 (source locators: 10, 10). Narrative conceptual review of human causal/blame judgments and debiasing, followed by secondary COMPAS and Berkeley fairness illustrations. It reports no newly recruited human sample, new AI benchmark, systematic review search or independently reproduced intervention effect. Human heuristics and formal algorithmic fairness constraints are not interchangeable.

name: Nudging
definition: Influencing choices by changing how options are presented or made accessible while preserving meaningful alternatives.
